# @alexify/syncom

> Fast, zero-dependency distributed data sync engine for JavaScript. Records
> are stored locally (node:fs, OPFS, IndexedDB, memory), every write is an op in
> a persisted log that peers replicate over an injected transport (wrpc over
> WebSocket or WebRTC) and that converges without a coordinator; schema
> validation, Mango queries, an optional hash-linked chain — one API across
> Node.js and the browser.

## Key facts

- Package: `@alexify/syncom` (npm), MIT, source at https://github.com/Alexis-Technologies/syncom
- Requires Node.js >= 22, or a browser with OPFS and Web Crypto (secure context)
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** Browser bundle is about 41 KB min+gzip (a CI budget); the wrpc adapter and the
  search index under 1 KB each
- CommonJS, no build step; `src/` ships as published; version 0.0.1 — a pre-release, not on npm, API may still change
- Entry points: `.` (Node `index.js` / browser `browser.js` via the `browser` export condition), `./wrpc`,
  `./contracts`, `./idb`, `./search`
- Exports: `open`, `Storage`, `SyncManager`, `isSyncLink`, `OpLog`, `applyOp`, `mergeEntry`, `isAlive`,
  `Blockchain`, `diff`, `merge`, `apply`, `calculateHash`, `generateKeys`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `loadKeys`,
  `generateSigningKeys`, `loadSigningKeys`, `sign`, `verify`,
  `read`, `write`, `exists`, `remove`, `list`, `isFsi`, `createMemoryFsi`, `HookError`, `ValidationError`,
  `SyncomError`, `isSharedLog`
- `@alexify/syncom/search` exports `createSearch`, `normalize`, `trigrams` — the trigram index for
  `open({ search })`; an entity's `search: [...]` fields are queried with `select({ $text: 'words' })`, best first
- `@alexify/syncom/wrpc` exports `createWrpcLink`, `isSyncLink`, `SYNC_INTROSPECTION`;
  `@alexify/syncom/contracts` exports `SmartContract`, `DataReader`; `@alexify/syncom/idb` exports `createIdbFsi`
- Every operational error is a `SyncomError` with a `code`
- `Storage`, `Blockchain`, `SyncManager` and `OpLog` initialise asynchronously: `await new Blockchain(path)`
- In the browser `calculateHash`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `sign` and `verify` return promises; in Node.js they are synchronous
- Every op is signed (Ed25519) by its origin, and the node id IS the origin's public key (base64url), so any
  peer verifies through any relay; `open({ sync: { signatures: 'verify' | 'require' | false } })` — only
  'require' refuses unsigned ops
- Every write is an op: `write` (insert/set), `set` (update/swap/record.save), `inc` (counters), `add`/`remove`
  (observed-remove sets, read sorted by element text), `delete` (tombstone). A field is a last-writer-wins
  register, a per-origin counter OR a set — one kind only; mixing throws
- Replication: every node dials the nodes in its registry through `sync.connect(node)` and hosts
  `storage.sync.unit()`; ops relay hop by hop, de-duplicated by version vector; a peer that cannot be
  resumed bootstraps from a snapshot. wrpc is injected, never a dependency
- `merge` ADDS numbers rather than replacing them — this is the counter CRDT and is deliberate; storage
  does not replicate through `merge`
- Encrypted records (`encrypted: true`) are sealed for this node's key and never leave it
- Scopes: a host drops the ops a peer may not write and serves only the scopes it was granted;
  `purge(id)` scrubs a payload out of the op log; `open({ chain: false })` keeps no chain

## Documentation

- [Why syncom?](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/why): what it is for, what sets it apart, when something else fits better.
- [Compared with alternatives](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/comparison): a 40-feature matrix against Yjs, Automerge, Loro, Jazz, RxDB, PouchDB, TinyBase, Dexie Cloud, Fireproof, GUN, OrbitDB, Evolu, LiveStore, ElectricSQL, PowerSync, Zero, Triplit and InstantDB.
- [Benchmarks](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/benchmarks): insert, update, read, counters, batches, replication, cold start and bundle size against nine libraries, plus syncom's own benchmarks.
- [Architecture](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/architecture): the facade, the three write paths, replication between nodes, the files on disk.
- [Getting Started](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/getting-started): install, open a storage, records, validation, a first sync.
- [Storage](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/storage): explicit API, registers, counters and sets, compare-and-swap, records, references, schema collections, encryption at rest, on-disk layout.
- [Sync](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/sync): the operation model, the log and its two cursors, signatures, the protocol, bootstrap, scopes, the registry, the link contract, guarantees and limits.
- [wrpc transport](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/wrpc): hosting `storage.sync.unit()` on a wrpc server, dialing with `createWrpcLink`, the browser, rooms and presence.
- [CRDT deltas](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/crdt): diff/merge/apply semantics, grow-only sets, the numeric-addition rule.
- [Schema and validation](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/schema): entity definitions, validators, versions and lenses, `migrate()`.
- [Queries](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/query): Mango `select()`, the catalog, indexes, unique keys, `watch()`, full-text `$text`.
- [Lists, text and trees](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/lists): list and text fields that merge by position (Fugue), the movable list, rich text marks, cursors, `updateText()`, trees whose moves never form a cycle.
- [Versions and history](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/versions): `history(id)` and `get(id, { at })` — by event id, stamp or version vector; tags, diff and restore, the commit event, undo and redo (`@alexify/syncom/undo`); what the log can vouch for after compaction.
- [Hooks and events](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/hooks): hooks inside writes, reads and peer batches; events.
- [Backends](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/backends): the `fsi` contract, node:fs, OPFS, IndexedDB, memory, the lock.
- [Scaling](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/scaling): hubs, scopes as buckets, limits, presence.
- [WebRTC](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/webrtc): browser peers through wrpc's PeerLink and PeerHost.
- [OpenTelemetry](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/telemetry): injected spans and metrics.
- [Blockchain log](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/chain): block structure, hash linking, validate cost, per-record verification.
- [Smart contracts](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/contracts): storing procedures in the chain, DataReader, the `new Function` risk, serialisation limits.
- [Browser](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/guide/browser): OPFS and Web Crypto, the async signature differences, bundle size.
- [API reference](https://syncomjs.vercel.app/reference/api): every export with signatures and return types.
